acceptance: Every tag used in docs/ and blog/ is either in a category, listed on an index section for uncategorised tags, or removed or merged into an existing tag in front matter, decided per tag
A converter test fails when a page uses a tag that no browse path reaches
The built tag index links every tag page that exists
context:
Noticed during the MyST retirement (PRs #112 to #114); recounted 2026-11-07: 145 tags, 65 uncategorised.

2026-11-07: Done in PR #131 (merge 37f4919815). tag-categories.ts gains five categories (data format, deployment, workload, results and analysis, maturity) and more tags in platform, benchmark and platform-type; browseCategories() in tag-pages.ts appends an 'Other Tags' category for any tag no category lists, used by the tag index, category pages and sidebar (currently 9 leftovers). Category-tag pattern now allows underscores. tag-pages.test.ts covers leftover placement, no Other Tags when all are categorised, and a build of the assembled docs fails if a tag page is missing from the index or sidebar. All 156 tags that have a page are reachable. Left: docs/index.md still links the original six category pages; about 50 blog-only tags have no pages by design; generator underscore tags (tpch_skew etc.) come from core. Only front matter edit: questdb timeseries to time-series.
description: Docs and blog front matter use 145 distinct tags; 65 of them (for example accelerated, ai-ml, analysis, benchmarks, beta, cedardb, citus, cloud-native, columnstore, comparison, credentials) are in no TAG_CATEGORIES entry in website/src/converter/tag-categories.ts. The tag index (_tags/tagsindex.md) and the category pages list only categorised tags, so those tags have pages but no browse path from the index or the sidebar's tag categories.
